verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Lean states the bound as an operator norm of a bilinear map, ‖inverseMixed I hε r hr‖ ≤ 5120/ε, not pointwise; two applications of the operator-norm inequality give ‖inverseMixed A B‖ ≤ (5120/ε)·‖A‖·‖B‖, which is (B.6) with the paper's unnamed C_ρ realised as the explicit 5120/ρ. The norms coincide: weight ε n m is (B.4)'s 𝔞_{αβ} and axisSpace_norm_le_iff is the printed quotient norm, with Lean's ε the paper's ρ. The operand matches: inverseMixed is built as one composite (jet_inverseMixed: convolution with ∂_η on the first factor, the degree factor j = D_Y on the second, divided by (n+1)(n+r)), and inverseMixed_actual_equation verifies Y u_YY + r u_Y = (∂_η F)(Y ∂_Y G), i.e. u = J_ν[(∂_η F)(D_X G)] with u(0,η)=0 (inverseMixed_axis_zero, line 377); D_X = X∂_X = Y∂_Y is the paper's own identification. Lean's hypothesis is 1 ≤ r, more general than the paper's ν ∈ {1,2}.
